name: Cuba
note: Traveler-focused Cuba pack (civil-law). Emergencies, police/ID, if detained, severe drug laws, mandatory health insurance, currency/import bans, driving (accidents = crimes), entry/visa, consular. Verify; not local legal advice.

getLawyer.why: In Cuba, expect to be held for the ENTIRE investigation — charges aren't laid until it's complete, delays are long, and you cannot leave the country meanwhile. Canadian citizenship gives no immunity. Ask to contact the Embassy of Canada, insist on a lawyer and an interpreter (police may speak only Spanish), and sign nothing without counsel. Dual citizens: if Cuba considers you Cuban, Canada may be unable to help.
Penalties for possession, use, or trafficking are SEVERE — lengthy prison sentences. Contact the embassy and get a Cuban lawyer immediately; say and sign nothing without counsel and an interpreter.

A traffic accident causing injury or death is treated as a CRIME in Cuba — the driver must prove innocence and a serious at-fault crash can bring up to 10 years in prison. Do not leave the scene, do not move the vehicle, call police (106), and contact the embassy and a lawyer. You may be barred from leaving until claims are paid.

deadlines.title: Tourist visa — 90 days (max 6 months total)
deadlines.rule: Canadians need a tourist visa (usually included in packages/direct flights); it allows up to 90 DAYS, extendable up to 6 MONTHS total by request. Travelling via a third country requires a Cuban e-visa in advance. Submit the D'Viajeros customs form up to 72 hours before arrival (QR code required). You must show proof of medical insurance on arrival.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Cuba

deadlines.title: Victims: get a 'comprobante de denuncia' before leaving
deadlines.rule: If you're the victim of a crime (incl. sexual assault), report it to Cuban authorities and obtain a 'comprobante de denuncia' (proof of complaint) BEFORE leaving Cuba — without a formal complaint, a criminal investigation may not be possible.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Cuba

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (Cuba)
sentencing.mandatory_minimum: Detention for the whole investigation; cannot leave the country.
sentencing.first_offender: Severe penalties even for possession/use; lengthy prison sentences. A local lawyer is essential.
sentencing.maximum: Lengthy imprisonment, served in Cuban prisons.
sentencing.collateral: Long pre-charge detention, exit ban, deportation.

sentencing.name: At-fault traffic accident with injury/death (Cuba)
sentencing.mandatory_minimum: Treated as a crime; driver must prove innocence; detention likely.
sentencing.first_offender: A serious at-fault accident can bring imprisonment and an exit ban until claims are paid.
sentencing.collateral: Exit ban, vehicle held, claims payable before departure.

statutes.title: Carry ID at all times
statutes.summary: You must legally carry valid ID at all times and officials can ask to see it anytime. Keep a photocopy of your passport and digital copies of your documents. Health insurance proof is mandatory on arrival; unpaid medical bills (cash USD only) must be settled before you can leave.

statutes.title: Banned/restricted items + currency
statutes.summary: Banned: satellite phones, drones (confiscated on entry), e-cigarettes/vapes (seized on arrival). GPS devices may be held until exit. You cannot leave with more than US$5,000 (or equivalent) or 5,000 CUP. Changing money outside authorized outlets is illegal. Photographing military/police/port/rail/airport sites is prohibited, and all anti-government demonstrations are illegal.

statutes.title: Consular access (limits)
statutes.summary: If detained, ask to contact the Embassy of Canada. Canadian officials cannot interfere in Cuban legal/judicial matters. Dual citizenship is NOT recognized — if Cuba treats you as a citizen, consular help may be refused.

book.title: Police, detention, and your rights in Cuba
book.overview: Cuba is a civil-law country where Canadian citizenship gives NO special protection. If detained, expect to be held for the whole investigation (long delays, no leaving the country) before charges are even laid. Carry ID always. Insist on the Embassy of Canada, a lawyer, and an interpreter. Emergencies: 106 police, 104 ambulance, 105 fire.
your_rights: You must carry ID; officials can ask anytime.
If detained, ask to contact the Embassy of Canada.
Ask for a lawyer and an interpreter (police may speak only Spanish).
Do not sign anything you don't understand or without a lawyer.
If you're a crime victim, get a 'comprobante de denuncia' before leaving.
key_steps: Carry ID and keep photocopies/digital copies.
Carry proof of medical insurance (mandatory on arrival).
If detained: ask for the embassy, a lawyer, an interpreter; stay calm.
Avoid demonstrations, street money-changing, and banned items (drones, sat phones, vapes).
common_mistakes: Expecting a quick release — detention lasts the whole investigation.
Not getting a formal complaint before leaving after a crime.
Assuming dual citizenship gets Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately for any arrest, drug matter, or serious traffic accident — contact the embassy and get a Cuban lawyer; you may be barred from leaving.

book.title: Entry, visa, and your stay in Cuba
book.overview: Canadians need a tourist visa (usually in the package/flight) for up to 90 days, extendable to 6 months total. Travel via a third country needs a Cuban e-visa. Submit the D'Viajeros customs form up to 72 hours before arrival (QR code). Proof of medical insurance is mandatory on arrival.
your_rights: Tourist visa up to 90 days; extendable to 6 months total.
You're entitled to entry once requirements are met.
You can request an extension beyond 90 days.
key_steps: Confirm your visa is included or get an e-visa if transiting a third country.
Submit the D'Viajeros form (≤72h before arrival); save the QR code.
Carry proof of medical insurance and valid passport.
Keep cash — Visa/Mastercard no longer accepted (from 6 Jun 2026).
common_mistakes: Assuming cards work (they don't since 6 Jun 2026).
No proof of insurance on arrival.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays or detention, consult a Cuban lawyer via the embassy.

book.title: Driving in Cuba — accidents are treated as crimes
book.overview: Car insurance is mandatory for foreign drivers. A traffic accident causing injury or death is a CRIME: the driver must prove innocence, and a serious at-fault crash can bring up to 10 years in prison. You may be barred from leaving until claims are paid.
your_rights: You can drive with mandatory insurance.
After a crash you have the right to a lawyer and the embassy.
You're entitled to a receipt when returning a rental.
key_steps: After any crash: do NOT leave the scene or move the vehicle; call police (106).
Contact the embassy and a lawyer immediately.
Keep rental receipts; expect possible exit holds until claims settle.
Avoid driving after dark; never pick up hitchhikers; avoid scooters.
common_mistakes: Leaving the scene of an accident.
Driving after drinking (common locally, still illegal).
book.when_lawyer: Immediately after any injury/fatal accident — it's a criminal matter; get the embassy and a lawyer.

book.title: Staying safe + legal traps in Cuba
book.overview: Emergencies: 106/104/105. The biggest legal traps: severe drug laws, banned items (drones, satellite phones, vapes), illegal street money-changing, photographing restricted sites, and anti-government demonstrations (all illegal — being near one can mean detention). Report any crime and get a formal complaint before you leave.
your_rights: The embassy has a 24/7 Emergency Watch & Response line.
You can report crime and obtain a 'comprobante de denuncia'.
key_steps: Exchange money only at authorized outlets.
Don't bring banned items (drones, sat phones, vapes).
After a crime, file a formal complaint before departure.
common_mistakes: Flying a drone or carrying a vape.
book.when_lawyer: For any detention, drug allegation, or serious crime, contact the embassy for local lawyer help.
